faqs.question: Is the Jupiter EDGE+ Credit Card lifetime free?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Jupiter EDGE+ Credit Card has no joining fee and no annual fee.

faqs.question: What is the forex markup on the Jupiter EDGE+ Credit Card?
faqs.answer: It's 2% plus GST on spends in a foreign currency. That's lower than the usual 3.5%, which helps when you spend abroad.

faqs.question: Does the Jupiter EDGE+ Credit Card give airport lounge access?
faqs.answer: No. The Jupiter EDGE+ Credit Card doesn't include free airport lounge access.

faqs.question: How much can I earn with the Jupiter EDGE+ Credit Card?
faqs.answer: You earn about 1% back in reward points on regular spends, and up to 10% on its bonus categories. Check the review above for the exact categories and monthly caps.

program_updates_2026: However, the actual rewards are tied to Jupiter’s Jewels program, and the headline reward rates do not apply to every transaction. From 10 October 2026, the top shopping rate also depends on spending more than ₹15,000 in a statement cycle. So, how rewarding is the card in day-to-day use?

From 10 October 2026, the 50% Jewels rate on partner shopping brands is no longer automatic. Every eligible shopping transaction now earns 5% Jewels instantly. The remaining 45% Jewels are credited at the end of the statement cycle only if your total eligible spends for that cycle are more than ₹15,000. If you fall short, the extra Jewels are cancelled.

One important thing to know is that the rewards program was devalued from 1 June 2026. Previously, all redemption options offered the same value of ₹0.20 per Jewel. After the change, statement credit and bill payment redemptions were reduced to ₹0.14 per Jewel, while vouchers, digital gold, and Jupiter Flights continue to offer ₹0.20 per Jewel.

Today, the card still offers strong rewards on partner brands and UPI transactions, but the headline reward rates are achievable only if you redeem Jewels through higher-value options such as vouchers or Jupiter Flights. If your preferred redemption method is statement credit, your effective returns are roughly 30% lower than before the devaluation.
